hero.tagline: One patient. A unique tumor. A real chance.
hero.title: Miriam has metastatic neuroendocrine breast cancer with a multi-resistant profile and standard medicine has no answers for her case.
hero.subtitle: Her tumor doesn't respond to any standard treatment. Finding the right one requires tests that public healthcare won't fund. And time cannot wait.

gofundme.title: Why do we need your help?
gofundme.subtitle: Miriam needs to fund a precision diagnostic strategy that public healthcare doesn't cover. Every contribution brings her case closer to an answer — and could set a precedent for other patients with tumours outside clinical guidelines.
gofundme.what_intro: The money covers the needs of the case as they emerge — not just one test, but everything involved in finding the right treatment for a tumour with no established protocol.
what_items: Bone re-biopsy with advanced genomic panel
Functional immunohistochemistry tests to identify therapeutic targets
Consultations and second opinions with international specialists
Clinical documentation for access to trials and compassionate use programmes
Any additional test that arises throughout the process
gofundme.why_title: Why isn't this covered by public healthcare?
gofundme.why_text: Guidelines still file many such cases as "standard HR+", but in 2026 this is stage IV neuroendocrine breast carcinoma (bone) with ctDNA showing three RB1 alterations and ESR1 D538G — a biological signature of resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors and aromatase targeting. That requires workups and decisions aligned with the NE phenotype, not only the luminal playbook.
gofundme.transparency_text: Every expense is publicly documented. We request quotes from international reference centers and share them with the community.

entry_disclaimer.title: Neuroendocrine breast carcinoma (BC-NED) with a multi-resistant profile (altered RB1 and ESR1 in plasma). Urgent need for non-luminal targeted therapy.
entry_disclaimer.body: Guardant360 and the VHIO/SOLTI report (April 2026) provide the resistance evidence: three RB1 alterations — a key mechanism versus CDK4/6 inhibitors such as abemaciclib — and ESR1 p.D538G (VAF 0.24%), consistent with first-line letrozole failure. FGFR1 and CCND1 amplifications persist (reported plasma copy numbers ~6.95 and ~7.63). Current clinical and pathology diagnosis (Hospital Morales Meseguer, April–May 2026): "stage IV neuroendocrine breast carcinoma (bone disease)." The 30/04/2026 bone biopsy may be falsely negative ("no neoplasia identified"); third-line strategy therefore rests on ctDNA, clinical correlation, and PET-CT showing clear progression (e.g. SUVmax up to 9.43 in the femur).

ciencia.proposed_panel_caption: Proposed re-biopsy panel: components, methods, targets and clinical implication
ciencia.goal_n_of_1_desc: A trial where Miriam is the sole unit of analysis, with decisions driven by plasma biology (RB1, ESR1, FGFR1/CCND1) and the formal NE diagnosis, not the generic HR+ label. The pathway prioritises tumour board review with integrated reading: SSTR imaging (Ga-68 DOTATOC/TATE PET when appropriate), radioligand therapy with Lu-177-DOTATATE or Ac-225 options when receptor biology supports it, and bridging options cited on liquid biopsy reports for approved neuroendocrine pathways (e.g. surufatinib and FGFR axis).
ciencia.win_consortium_desc: WIN Consortium (Worldwide Innovative Network in Oncology) is an international network connecting centres of excellence in precision oncology to design personalised diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
ciencia.win_consortium_precedent: This would set a precedent: precision oncology adapted to each patient, without bureaucracy around the primary tumor.
ciencia.why_no_fit_guidelines: Why doesn't this tumor fit the guidelines?
ciencia.why_no_fit_guidelines_text: In 2026 pathology reads as stage IV neuroendocrine breast carcinoma (bone). ctDNA shows likely RB1 loss-of-function (three variants) and endocrine resistance (ESR1 D538G), with FGFR1/CCND1 maintained: biologically this is no longer standard luminal disease that can be met with further hormone-only plus CDK4/6 rotation. National pathways often lag the NE breast algorithms that NCCN/ENETS describe for SSTR imaging and PRRT.
ciencia.therapeutic_case_reading_p1: Phenotypic switch: as classical luminal routes fail (ESR1 in plasma and altered RB1), tumour growth can be sustained by the dominant neuroendocrine programme. That links first- and second-line failure to current biology and to the formal neuroendocrine breast carcinoma diagnosis.
ciencia.therapeutic_case_reading_p2: SSTR targeting: recognising NE disease supports requesting somatostatin analogue PET (Ga-68 DOTATOC/TATE). If uptake is positive, Lu-177-DOTATATE or Ac-225-based radioligand approaches are justified by receptor biology relative to breast origin alone.
ciencia.therapeutic_case_reading_p3: Options flagged on the liquid report (e.g. surufatinib, with FGFR1 relevance in approved neuroendocrine settings) can serve as a therapeutic bridge and as committee-facing rationale when the luminal algorithm is closed by documented resistance.
ciencia.thesis: The thesis: biology, not the organ of origin, should guide treatment.
ciencia.thesis_goal: Goal: an N-of-1 trial that sets a precedent for precision oncology in ultra-rare subtypes.

team.title: The team
team.subtitle: A multidisciplinary group that formed spontaneously around a common goal
team.how_it_formed: This team wasn't planned. It formed organically when professionals from different fields (technology, medicine, AI, research) saw a case that challenged them and decided to contribute what they knew. There is no formal hierarchy. There is a shared goal: let this tumor's biology guide treatment.

historia.story_teaser_1: Three years ago, Miriam was working full-time as a software developer and creating content about technology. Within a matter of months, her life took a radical turn.
historia.story_teaser_2: It all began with back pain, physiotherapy sessions and GPs who couldn't find a solution. As the pain persisted and the healthcare system offered no answers, she decided to arrange an MRI scan herself. One Thursday in January 2024, she found the test results in her inbox: «probable vertebral metastases». The case later evolved to the formal 2026 diagnosis: «stage IV neuroendocrine breast carcinoma (bone disease)».
historia.story_teaser_3: For two years, Miriam has been rebuilding her life piece by piece with treatments that have given her time and peace of mind, but with an end date. In 2026, everything has moved forward at breakneck speed. What if these advances, combined with the specific nature of her cancer, opened doors that previously seemed closed?
historia.story_teaser_4: In this story, we want to tell you about Míriam's case, her journey and her daily routine so that you can truly understand what it means to live with stage 4 cancer.
